reason: The passage explicitly presents shepherding (רעיה) as a model for good leadership. God directly tells David 'you will shepherd (תִרְעֶה) My people Israel,' using the shepherd metaphor which inherently denotes caring for the welfare of those under one's care. This is reinforced by David's selection: the tribes identify him as one who 'leads them out and brings them in,' indicating active care for the people's wellbeing. The passage further demonstrates this through David's distribution of food and provisions to all the people 'from each man to each woman,' showing concrete acts of providing for their welfare. The shepherd metaphor was a standard ancient Near Eastern model for describing a leader's responsibility to care for those entrusted to them.
